purpose: Record Batanes inland-water and aquaculture leads, distinguish cage culture and island-level historical vocabulary from wild fish occurrence, and keep lake-name reconciliation open.

waterbodyLead.locality: Itbayat, Batanes; BFAR newsletter associates the fish-cage demonstration with the Raele Fisherfolk Association.
waterbodyLead.classAsReported: lake / freshwater waterbody used for cage culture
identityLimits: BFAR Region II's 2022 newsletter names Kayaywan Lake for the tilapia cage-culture demonstration.
The 2024 BFAR provincial profile reports one lake covering 22 hectares in Batanes but does not name it or give a map; do not assume the count is a verified identity crosswalk to Kayaywan Lake.

A 2024 PIA story places the sole freshwater lake described as suitable for aquaculture in Barangay Reale, Itbayat, but does not name the lake. BFAR reports the Itbayat barangay as Raele in its hatchery story; the Reale/Raele spelling difference remains source-attributed and unresolved.
No geometry, shoreline, coordinate, datum, or lake feature ID was retrieved.

documentedCultureEvidence.sourceReportedEvent: BFAR Region II's July–December 2022 newsletter reports two tilapia cage-culture technology-demonstration projects in Kayaywan Lake, says cage farming was introduced in Itbayat in 2016, and reports a 312 kg harvest after a four-month culture period sold to nearby communities.
documentedCultureEvidence.evidenceClass: managed aquaculture / culture harvest, not a wild-fish survey
documentedCultureEvidence.taxonLimit: The source says tilapia without a scientific species identification, stock source, or voucher.

documentedCultureEvidence.sourceReportedEvent: A Philippine Information Agency report dated 2024-04-16 describes Itbayat's first municipal tilapia hatchery in Barangay Reale, beside the sole freshwater lake it calls suitable for aquaculture. It reports a projected 300,000–500,000 fingerlings per year; this is a projection, not verified production or lake stocking.
documentedCultureEvidence.evidenceClass: aquaculture facility and projected hatchery output, not a lake fish survey

additionalNameAndHistoricalContext.sourceReportedEvent: BFAR Region 02's 2024 Annual Report says Mr. Juan Ibañez received tilapia fingerlings for his fish cage at Kavaywan Lake, Raele, Itbayat, Batanes.
additionalNameAndHistoricalContext.evidenceClass: fish-cage/aquaculture distribution context, not a wild-fish record or lake-boundary source

nameCrosswalkCandidate.relationship: Possible spelling/name variant because both sources describe Itbayat freshwater fish-cage activity, but no source explicitly equates the features.

additionalNameAndHistoricalContext.placeNameCaveat: The BFAR form Raele and the PIA form Reale are retained as source-attributed spellings. The reports do not establish an official barangay-name crosswalk or prove which lake is meant.
additionalNameAndHistoricalContext.areaCrosswalkCaveat: The same BFAR report's page 47 lists one Batanes lake at 22 hectares without naming it; do not assume it is Kayaywan/Kavaywan or the Reale/Raele lake.

historicalFreshwaterContext.finding: A 1967 Itbayat fishing-vocabulary article lists freshwater labels dalag (mudfish), tilapia (described as introduced recently in its historical context), and tuna (printed as Anguilla mauritiana Bennett).
historicalFreshwaterContext.relationshipToNamedLakes: Island-level historical ethnographic context only. The source names no freshwater body and is not linked to Kayaywan Lake, Kavaywan Lake, the Reale/Raele lake, or the 22-hectare provincial lake.
historicalFreshwaterContext.taxonomicLimit: Dalag and tilapia are unresolved labels. A Catalog of Fishes name cross-check treats Anguilla mauritiana as a synonym of Anguilla marmorata while noting prior competing treatments; this does not re-identify an unvouchered historical local-name record.

regionalProfileContext.finding: The BFAR Region II 2024 annual report's Batanes provincial profile lists one lake and 22 hectares. It does not name the lake, say whether the area is seasonal, provide geometry, or report a fish checklist.
regionalProfileContext.use: Provincial-scale freshwater inventory context only; not a named-waterbody boundary or fish evidence.

interpretationLimits: Caged tilapia harvest is not evidence of wild tilapia presence, natural diet, abundance, or present-day status in Kayaywan Lake.
The two cage projects and the later hatchery are aquaculture infrastructure; do not merge cage/tank culture records with a wild species checklist.

Kayaywan, Kavaywan, Reale, and Raele are source-reported name forms. Similar spelling and Itbayat aquaculture context make them crosswalk candidates, not proof that all names identify the same feature. The provincial one-lake/22-hectare summary is unnamed and remains unlinked.
Yamada's 1967 Itbayat fish labels are historical ethnographic vocabulary, not a modern survey or a waterbody-resolved fish observation; keep them separate from cage-culture evidence.
No water quality, safety, fishing access, catchability, legal, or public-app claim is supported by these sources.
followUp: Continue with independently accessible literature, museum catalogues, biodiversity indexes, university repositories, and archival maps for voucher-backed or method-described wild-fish evidence in Batanes lakes and streams; do not wait on a government response and do not treat bounded search results as evidence of absence.

Resolve Reale/Raele and Kayaywan/Kavaywan spellings only if a publicly accessible primary map, gazetteer, or other independent source explicitly links the names; do not create a geometry or alias from spelling similarity alone.
Keep cage-production evidence and island-level historical vocabulary separate from wild-fish survey records.

sources.supports: BFAR Region II July–December 2022 newsletter: Kayaywan Lake tilapia cage-culture demonstration, start of Itbayat cage culture in 2016, and a reported 312 kg four-month culture harvest.

Page 9 names Kavaywan Lake, Raele in the context of tilapia fingerlings for a fish cage; page 47 lists one Batanes lake covering 22 hectares without naming or mapping it. Neither passage provides a wild fish survey or resolves whether the lake names match.
Historical island-level freshwater vocabulary labels only; see the separate review for taxonomy and locality limits.
Itbayat tilapia hatchery in Barangay Reale and source-reported sole freshwater lake suitable for aquaculture; hatchery output is a projection.
